title: Geologists everywhere use two Hawaiian words for lava: pāhoehoe and ʻaʻā
body: Runny basalt lava sets in two very different ways, and geology borrowed the Hawaiian names for both. **Pāhoehoe** (“smooth, unbroken lava”) cools into a smooth, billowy or ropy skin, and a flow creeps forward as small lobes and toes that keep breaking out of its cooled crust. **ʻAʻā** (“stony rough lava”) is usually stiffer and ends up as a jumble of broken blocks called clinker. Pāhoehoe can turn into ʻaʻā when it becomes turbulent, for example on steep slopes or when it meets obstacles.

cover.alt: A lobe of fresh silvery lava with glowing orange edges spreading over older dark grey lava

slides.alt: Real-time close-up of a pāhoehoe lava breakout: a wrinkled silvery lobe of lava swells and creeps over older black lava, its edges glowing orange where new toes of molten rock push out.
slides.caption: A pāhoehoe breakout on Kīlauea’s “61g” flow, Hawaiʻi, 12 August 2016, at actual speed: glowing toes keep bursting out of the cooling crust.

left.label: Pāhoehoe
left.text: A smooth, billowy or ropy skin; runnier; creeps along in lobes and toes

right.label: ʻAʻā
right.text: A rough rubble of broken blocks called clinker; usually stiffer

slides.heading: Typical temperature as they erupt
slides.note: Typical ranges; ʻaʻā sometimes erupts hotter than 1,150 °C

slides.label: of Kīlauea buried by flows like this one
slides.text: By 2016, countless pāhoehoe flows from the Puʻu ʻŌʻō eruption, which began in 1983, had covered that much land, according to the USGS.

slides.heading: Pāhoehoe or ʻaʻā?

items.text: Advances as small lobes and toes
Covered in broken blocks called clinker
Can build lava tubes that keep it hot and runny

slides.explanation: Pāhoehoe is the smooth, runny kind that creeps along in toes and builds lava tubes; ʻaʻā is the stiffer, rubbly kind.

slides.question: Pāhoehoe can turn into ʻaʻā. What makes it change?
slides.explanation: When pāhoehoe becomes turbulent, on steep slopes or by running into obstacles, it can turn into rubbly ʻaʻā.
